tasks.question: My tractor has a standard PWM-style hydraulic steering valve, and I am planning an AIO full-autosteer build. How should I decide whether to reuse its wheel-angle sensor or buy a Land Rover sensor, plan the sensor and Ampseal harness wiring, and check the other hardware choices before ordering?

I have ordered an AIO board and want to assemble it for a single-antenna setup with an IMU and a DIY steering motor. What parts and compatibility checks should I make before assembling the board and cab components?
I have an unassembled V4 AIO board and want to bring up its Teensy and a single F9P receiver. What should I check, assemble, configure, and look for on the board before I try steering?

I’m setting up AgOpenGPS and AgIO with an Ethernet-connected AIO Teensy and an RTK caster for a simulator bench session. How should I get the software, module connection, and correction path working, and what should I check if AgIO shows a connection problem?

I have an Ethernet-capable module connected to my Windows computer and an NTRIP caster account. How do I bring up the module and RTK connection in AgIO, then check the setup if the module still shows red?

I maintain a standalone role with custom plugins and want to distribute it as certified Ansible content. How should I migrate it into a collection, prepare the collection for publication, and update references to the role and plugins?

I manage Windows Server 2019 and 2022 hosts and need to roll out 7-Zip through Ansible. Most hosts use WinRM, some use domain Kerberos, and we are considering SSH and Windows App Control for subsets of the fleet. What installation and connection approach should I use, what must I prepare on each path, and how can I check that the rollout is ready?

I maintain a playbook for a mixed fleet. It needs release-specific input, repeated account setup, and configuration steps that apply only to certain hosts. How should I structure it and check its behavior before rollout?

Our team wants to integrate a third-party product API with Ansible and may contribute the result to a collection. How should we decide what to build, divide the functionality, and prepare a Python module contribution for review?

I maintain a large playbook that deploys configuration to web and database hosts. For a release, I need to run only the relevant configuration tasks, including tasks grouped in a block or role, then check the selected run and troubleshoot a failure. How should I set up and execute that workflow?

We are replacing routine use of Argo CD’s built-in admin account. Our platform team needs group-based permissions and CLI login. How should we choose an SSO integration path, configure the relevant identity claims and RBAC, and check the operational caveats before rollout?

I’m contributing an Argo CD resource tab that needs information from a separate backend service. How should I put together the UI and proxy configuration, and what should I check while developing and preparing the documentation change?

I’m contributing an Argo CD backend and UI change on macOS. How should I set up the development environment, choose a toolchain, run Argo CD locally against a development cluster, and prepare the change for review?

I maintain an Argo CD resource tab extension that needs data from our own service to display an anomaly view. How should I configure and deliver the integration, and what should I check before making it available to users?

We run a multi-tenant Argo CD instance and want tenant teams to create Applications while limiting the credentials used for their syncs. As the platform administrator, how should I decide whether to pilot sync impersonation, prepare a tenant for it, and set deployment controls before allowing team-managed Applications?

I’m contributing a fix to an existing Django admin JavaScript interaction and need to submit it for review. How should I prepare the branch, update the behavior and its QUnit tests, document any user-visible change, and check the contribution before opening a pull request?

I maintain a Django 1.3 application and am planning an upgrade to 1.7. What should I check across the intervening releases, and how should I decide whether its Python runtime, database schema workflow, time-zone handling, and older APIs are ready?

I’m planning a Django registration form that records a visitor’s details and sends a welcome email. What components and checks should I put in place, and how should I decide whether the email belongs in the form-handling flow or a signal?

I maintain a Django app deployed with a default database and a reporting database. We need a data migration that changes existing records only on the default database, then deploy it across our team, staging, and production. How should I write, route, apply, and verify it, and what should I check before deployment or rollback?

We have a Django view that makes several slow HTTP requests and may need to serve long-running responses. How should we move this endpoint to an async view, deploy it, and check that its existing response behavior still works?

I maintain a GitHub-hosted application and want Docker Hub to build and publish its image when I push to the main branch, but only after container tests pass. How should I set this up, verify the builds, and handle common failures, including a possible private submodule?

I maintain a Dockerfile that uses a base image and downloads a remote file. How should I set up a build policy so our builds accept images from approved registries and permit only HTTPS downloads, then check that the policy behaves as intended before using it in our builds?

I maintain a growing codebase and want a Docker Agent coding assistant in my ACP-capable editor to find relevant code by meaning without loading the whole repository into its prompt. How should I configure the searchable source and editor integration, then check that it works and choose sensible operating options?

Our organization has a DHI Select subscription and needs a FIPS variant of a Python image with an additional company certificate for a regulated service. As the platform engineer, how should I find and mirror the right repository, create the customized image, and check that the resulting image is suitable to hand to the application team?

I manage two application containers on one Linux Docker host. They need to reach each other by name, while a web endpoint should initially be reachable only from the host. How should I set up and check their networking, and what changes if we later need access from another host or have a legacy application that requires a physical-network identity?

I operate 7.17.x Elastic deployments on self-managed infrastructure, ECH, and ECE. How should I plan and carry out upgrades to the latest 9.x release, including component order, platform-specific preparation, and checks that could delay or interrupt production service?

I administer an Elastic Cloud Hosted deployment and need a recoverable snapshot before a deployment change. We may have to recover selected indices in a new deployment in another region. How should I prepare the repository and snapshot, then carry out and check the restore?

I manage host metrics in Fleet and am moving a System metrics collection from Metricbeat to Elastic Agent. I want the resulting data organized by environment, a new field added to the System CPU documents during ingest, and a retention policy applied only to the selected data streams. What should I configure and check?

I administer a self-managed Elasticsearch cluster and need a snapshot-based recovery plan before restoring selected indices and a data stream to another cluster for testing. S3 is our planned repository, Azure Blob storage is an alternative, and we may later use searchable snapshots for older data. What should I configure and check so the restore is usable and does not put cluster data or access at risk?

I’m planning the first startup of a self-managed, multi-node Elasticsearch cluster that must remain available if one master-eligible node fails. How should I assign roles, bootstrap the cluster, and check that later node changes will preserve availability?

We have an Express 4 app and want to upgrade it to Express 5 while adding CouchDB-backed endpoints for creating and listing books. What implementation and verification plan should our developer follow so requests complete and database failures reach Express error handling?

Our Express 4 API has GET and POST routes, request middleware, and asynchronous handlers. We are preparing an Express 5 upgrade for production. What migration and validation plan should our maintainer use to preserve request handling, surface errors, and check production concerns?

I'm adding a browser-facing POST endpoint to an Express app. How should I arrange route and middleware handling so requests can be parsed, traced, logged, checked for cookies, and either answered or passed to error handling?

I maintain an Express 3 API with a redirect endpoint, and we are preparing to make it publicly available. How should I plan an upgrade to a supported Express release, replace middleware that no longer comes with Express, check the relevant security fixes, and verify request and error handling? Include what changes if we choose Express 5.

Our production service still runs Express 3 and relies on its built-in body parsing, sessions, logging, and static files. What migration plan would get it onto a supported Express release while preserving request behavior and checking the release for known security issues?

We already use SAML SSO on GitHub Enterprise Server 3.14 or later and want to add SCIM through our own identity management system. What should our enterprise administrator check before enabling provisioning, and how should we handle and verify a departing employee’s access if they might later return?

I own an organization whose repositories use deploy keys in automated deployment. I want to restrict deploy keys without breaking deployments. How should I assess the current keys, choose replacement access, and sequence the change?

I use a personal GitHub account in the browser and need command line or API access for my own work. How should I choose and secure those credentials, handle an unexpected sign in prompt on a new device, and check that my existing sessions are legitimate?

I administer a repository whose protected base branch receives frequent pull requests. How should I configure reviewed merges through a merge queue, make sure CI does not block the queue, and check for rules that could interfere?

Our team is moving many repositories from GitHub Enterprise Server into an existing GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization, and we cannot take every repository down at once. How should a migration lead plan the migration units, assign the required access, run a trial, and check repository access and security afterward?

Several teams share our fixed-size Kubernetes cluster. How should I set namespace resource budgets so one team or one Pod cannot monopolize capacity, and how can I verify the controls when workloads are submitted?

I administer a kubeadm cluster with Linux and Windows worker nodes and need to plan its next supported minor-version upgrade. What sequence should I follow for the control plane and each worker type, and what checks or conditions could change that plan?

I'm migrating a replicated, stateless web service from a ReplicationController and need controlled container-image updates. Which workload resource should I use, how should I make and check a rollout, and what can I do if it becomes unstable? Flag whether the choice would change for a node-local log agent or a component that needs persistent Pod identity.

I administer a self-managed Kubernetes cluster that will run critical workloads. How should I choose a kubeadm high-availability topology and check that the proposed nodes and infrastructure are ready before setup?
I’m a new Kubernetes documentation contributor preparing a task page that walks readers through one procedure. How should I create the page, check it locally, and submit it for review?

We are moving a Next.js 16 app from `unstable_cache` to Cache Components. Product data is read by several server instances, some recommendations depend on request cookies, and users should see their own edits immediately while catalog updates can appear shortly afterward. What caching design should we implement, and how should we check its behavior?

I maintain a JavaScript App Router product section with a dynamic page, a shared layout, a route handler, and product metadata. How should I migrate it to TypeScript and verify that its production build remains type safe?

Our CMS-backed Next.js site is headed for a static-file host, but editors need draft previews, published pages should refresh without a full rebuild, an API endpoint accepts submissions, and traffic passes through a CDN. Is static export suitable for this deployment? Give us a deployment recommendation and the implementation and production checks needed for these features.

I maintain a Next.js 14 App Router app with TypeScript pages that read cookies, headers, route parameters, and server-fetched data. How should I move it through versions 15 and 16, and what should I check in those routes afterward?

Our growing Next.js app has slow local route compilation and rising memory use. We develop on Windows and sometimes use Docker. How should I diagnose the bottleneck and choose changes we can verify without confusing development behavior with production builds?

I maintain a training model with nn.Module hooks and mixed precision. After adding torch.compile, early runs are slow, a later run produces different gradients, and I may need to file a compiler issue. How should I isolate the cause, check whether the hooks and backward autocast are involved, and collect useful performance and reproduction evidence?

We are moving a Transformer training job from FSDP1 to FSDP2, want tensor parallelism across part of the device mesh, and need checkpoints that can resume under a different cluster topology. What implementation and validation plan should we use, including how to investigate a collective hang?

I maintain a library function compiled with `torch.compile`. It contains a tensor-dependent branch and calls a helper that Dynamo cannot trace; performance is below expectations. How should I locate and resolve the graph breaks, choose a suitable treatment for the helper, and validate that the compiled behavior remains correct?

Our compiled model receives varying batch sizes on multiple ranks, and its dynamic-shape behavior differs between jobs. How should I make those decisions reusable, inspect which inputs became dynamic, and diagnose remaining recompilations before deploying the change?

I maintain a trainable PyTorch module and need to add a custom C++ or CUDA operation on Windows. How should I prepare the build, connect the operation to the module and autograd, and check its behavior across CPU and GPU runs?

We’re enabling Strict Mode in an existing React app. During development, a memoized list calculation appears to run twice, state logs seem stale after updates, and a hideable sidebar has subscriptions. How should we enable the checks and decide which behavior is expected versus which code needs repair?

I'm building a CSS-in-JS-backed chat room that connects when the room or server changes, shows a notification using the current theme, and positions a tooltip from its measured height. How should I organize its Effects and refs so updates and cleanup behave correctly?

I’m building a reusable React form field with a controlled select, options supplied by its parent, and help text that may appear in several copies of the form. How should I wire the selection, submission value, and help text, and handle disabled or multiple-selection variants?

I have a designer's mockup and JSON product data for a searchable product table. How should I split it into React components, wire the search input to the displayed rows, and keep the implementation sound as it grows?

We maintain a TypeScript React 18 web app and are planning its React 19 upgrade. It has an older browser entry point, and some deployments hydrate server-rendered HTML. What migration plan should we follow, and what should we check in the entry points and tests before calling the upgrade complete?

Our Redis service has intermittent client-visible latency spikes. How should an on-call engineer investigate whether commands, Redis events, or the host are responsible, choose appropriate mitigations, and check whether performance improves?

Our team needs Redis running on an Ubuntu host, with developers using Windows and macOS. How should we install and verify the Ubuntu instance, secure its initial configuration, and choose workable local installation paths for the developers?

I operate a single-master Redis service with replicas, and my application must keep finding the writable master after a failure. How should I plan Sentinel-based failover, including replication and durability tradeoffs, client discovery, and production checks before rollout?

Our team has a small Redis bicycle-inventory prototype and is considering Go, Python, Node.js, and .NET backends. How should we compare the documented connection paths, verify basic reads and writes locally, and plan for a production connection?

Our Redis cache holds page fragments as strings alongside some small aggregate values, and memory use is growing. How should I set a memory cap, choose and check eviction behavior for our access pattern, and assess whether encoding changes are worthwhile on our Redis version?

I maintain a VS Code project where our coding conventions should apply in every chat, some rules should apply only to particular files, and we repeatedly run a review workflow. We also want a planning role that cannot edit code and a reusable workflow with scripts. How should I set up these customizations, and how can I check why a rule is not taking effect?

I need to let a VS Code agent work in a newly obtained project that contains sensitive configuration files and may require a third-party extension. What setup and review process should I use before trusting the project, running agent tools, and accepting its changes?

Our team repeatedly plans features in VS Code before handing them to an implementation agent. How should I set up a reusable planning workflow that keeps the planner's tools appropriate, lets us review and revise the plan, and carries the work into implementation?

I maintain a repository that needs a repeatable VS Code development environment. I also need to build and test the app in production-like containers from within that environment. How should I set up the dev container, choose a way to access Docker for testing, and confirm configuration changes take effect?

I’ve been assigned a feature in a GitHub repository and want to handle it from VS Code: get the repository locally, keep the feature separate from the main line, save my changes, and make the branch available to collaborators. What setup and workflow should I follow, including the checks that matter before syncing or merging?

population: 70 source-checked but human-unreviewed tasks at 14 CIKM anchor snapshots; development only
outbound_data_gate: Requires new explicit authorization for the full panel and its proposed $27 estimated-charge stop, plus fresh automatic review. Raising the software ceiling does not authorize spending.
